chapter: Inside the Basie rhythm section and band family
title: Staying out of the way of Basie, Jo Jones and Walter Page
summary: He explains how the three traded phrases and broke the rhythm while he kept time steady.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well, Freddie -- I mean -- that must have been -- I mean -- that really -- that was a rhythm section like there's never been a rhythm section like That in a band before.
I know, you know. But, I stayed out of the way -- now, because Jo Jones and Walter Page and Basie was doing something else. You see, I think --
You didn't stay out of the way -- you fell right in with them.
I think that's one of the reason I got out of their way. I think that's one of the reason I started, you know, playing --. Because they run into some [stick] thing, you know.
Yeah.
And, Basie would do something, and then Jo Jones would answer him --
Yeah.
-- and then Walter Page would come in.
Yeah.
So, I figured 'Well, if they did it, maybe it was my turn to come in, you know'. And, I went into something, and said 'no, no -- just keep time', you know. So who am I to say ?
(laugh)
So, I just, you know -- played rhythm.
Yeah.
Because, what they were doing, you know, was
something else. They would break the rhythm, you know.
Yeah.
I think -- like on that record they did -- What's that -- one of the early records they did?
The one with the small group with Totti where they did "Shoe Shine Boy" and "Lady Be Good".
Yeah. I think they've got some place in there where they break the rhythm up.
Yeah. They do.
They do. And, that's what they did, you see.
Yeah.
And I said -- well, I -- you know -- (laugh) "I'll just keep time while they're doing that, you know".
(laugh) Yeah.
Keep the time going while they're doing --
Well, that was precisely the point. That's what they needed.
Yeah.
Wasn't it? That's what they wanted. They wanted somebody that just was superb for keeping the time. Keeping the time that they needed.
Yeah. So, that's what I did.
